outcome_detail: No resolution reported as of mid-2026; 2026 coverage continues to describe the Baldwin-related suits as active lawsuits against the provincial government. In November 2022 a judge (Justice Peter O'Flaherty) denied retired Sgt. Robert Baldwin's application for a publication ban on his identity in the case.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges reported against Baldwin; coverage states the plaintiff was not pursuing criminal charges. NL's Serious Incident Response Team was reported in 2021 to be investigating sexual-offence allegations against several RNC officers, but no charges against Baldwin have been reported.
description: A Royal Newfoundland Constabulary officer filed a civil suit against the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, which is responsible for the force, alleging she was raped in 2014 by a colleague, Sgt. Robert Baldwin. The statement of claim, filed Jan. 13, 2022 and amended May 5, 2022 in the province's Supreme Court, alleges Baldwin was on duty in St. John's when he drove the off-duty officer home in his marked police vehicle after a night of drinking, invited himself into her home and raped her, and claims the province is vicariously liable. Baldwin, who has since retired and is not named as a defendant, denies the allegations in their entirety, according to court documents. In November 2022 the court denied Baldwin's application for a publication ban on his identity. The allegations have not been tested in court.
notes: Companion records from the same RNC scandal: rec-79 (seven-women suit, Sept. 2022) and rec-80/rec-80b (two suits filed March 2024, also naming Baldwin as alleged assailant). Plaintiff is a member of the force suing over assault by a colleague, coded 'internal' although the alleged assault occurred off-duty at her home rather than in the workplace.
